claims.reason: `hF` is an explicit binder of the theorem. Nothing else in the statement mentions it: `he` and the conclusion `IsZ2Periodic (fun x => gradMatrix F x i j)` elaborate without it. I checked the definitions. `Vec 2` is `Fin 2 → ℝ`. `gradMatrix F x i j` is `spaceGrad (fun y => F y j) x i`, which is `fderiv ℝ (fun y => F y j) x (basisVec i)`. `IsZ2Periodic g` means `∀ n x, g (x + latticeShift n) = g x`. So it is enough to show `fderiv ℝ f (x + L) = fderiv ℝ f x` with `f := fun y => F y j` and `L := latticeShift k`. Two Mathlib lemmas in FDeriv/Add.lean do this, and neither needs a differentiability hypothesis. `fderiv_comp_add_right (a : E) : fderiv 𝕜 (fun x ↦ f (x + a)) x = fderiv 𝕜 f (x + a)` rewrites the left side as `fderiv ℝ (fun y => F (y + L) j) x`. By `he`, funext and `Pi.add_apply`, that function equals `fun y => F y j + L j`. Then `fderiv_add_const (c : F) : fderiv 𝕜 (fun y => f y + c) x = fderiv 𝕜 f x` gives `fderiv ℝ (fun y => F y j) x`. Both sides then agree after applying them to `basisVec i`. The argument has no gap, so the theorem is still true and provable without `hF`.
